text:
taylor: Noticed a customer integration flake: their Node sample app retries on 502 but Python sample treats it as fatal. We don't have a single cross-SDK contract for errors right now. This is causing onboarding friction. Anyone up for defining a minimal normalized error?
nina: Seen this too. The telemetry shows divergent retry behavior depending on which SDK is used. We should make SDKs normalize transport-level failures into a predictable shape consumers can pattern-match on.
chet: Quick sketch: canonical envelope with fields: kind, code, http_status, retryable (bool), retry_after_seconds (optional), message, details_url (optional). SDKs expose a typed exception/object wrapping that envelope.
taylor: That matches my thoughts. Example problem in Node: we get an Error with message "502 Bad Gateway" and stack only. In Go we surface a RedwoodError with Code="internal_error" which makes it retryable, so the same upstream event is handled differently.
leo: Can we reuse any existing proto? We have an ErrorV1 in infra but it's incomplete for streaming and partial responses. Recommend ErrorV2 as the canonical schema and document streaming variants.
maria: For streaming, surface a StreamingInterrupted kind and include last_event_index and truncated boolean. Otherwise apps trying to resume streams can't tell if it's network vs model token-limit.
nina: Also need a status mapping table. Proposed defaults: 429 -> retryable=true, honor Retry-After if present; 503 -> retryable=true with exponential backoff; 500/502 -> retryable=true but be conservative; 4xx (except 429) -> retryable=false. We should include these in the spec but allow operator overrides.
chet: Add guidance to SDKs: normalize HTTP and gRPC transports into same envelope, map transport errors (DNS, TLS) to kind=transport_error with retryable=true by default but let the underlying error detail be preserved.
taylor: Action plan: 1) Draft spec PR in infra/error-contracts with schema + status table + streaming rules. 2) Add three tiny sample apps (python/node/go) that intentionally assert normalization for 429/500/502/503 and a simulated stream interruption. 3) SDK owners add normalization layer behind a feature flag. 4) Roll out with a minor semver bump and a migration guide.
leo: I'll own the spec PR and the streaming rules doc.
maria: I'll build the Python sample app and the test harness for stream interruptions. Include a short README on how to simulate Retry-After and transient failures.
nina: I'll coordinate Node SDK changes and add a small e2e test to the samples CI. Also add an opt-in env var REDWOOD_ERROR_SHAPE=stable for dogfooding.
chet: I'll update Go SDK and ensure our typed error implements helper methods: IsRetryable(), RetryAfter() -> time.Duration, Code(). Add unit tests asserting parity.
taylor: Testing matrix: unit tests for SDKs asserting envelope fields, sampleapp e2e asserting behavior across SDKs, and a migration note in release notes. Include a snippet for recommended backoff: exponential base 0.5s with jitter capped at 60s; always respect Retry-After.
maria: One UX question: how do we present this to customers? Suggest a short guide: "Error handling 101" in docs with patterns (retry vs fail-fast) and copy snippets.
leo: Agree. Add a compatibility section: old unnormalized exceptions will remain for one minor release with a compatibility shim that can be enabled. Then flip the default in the following minor.
nina: Ops-bot: can you add this as an agenda item for next devex sync?
ops-bot: Reminder: devex weekly Tue 10:00 — added item 'cross-SDK error normalization' (Ticket: DX-412).
taylor: Great. I'll open the tracking ticket with owners and PR links and ping the SDK leads once the spec is up. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
